Basic Information for CVE-2026-44490 Vulnerability Information Axios: DoS & Header Injection via Prototype Pollution Read-Side Gadgets in axios merge functions Overview Axios (a Promise-based HTTP client) has two Prototype Pollution gadgets involving reading through the prototype chain in versions prior to 0.32.0 and 1.16.0. When Object.prototype is polluted by an upstream dependency in the same process (such as lodash's _.merge / CVE-2018-16487), Axios silently picks up these polluted values, leading to sensitive data leakage or request interruption. Affected Versions Affected versions: Axios < 0.32.0 and Axios < 1.16.0 Fixed versions: Axios 0.32.0 and 1.16.0 Details Data Leakage Risk (lib/utils.js): In line 406, when building the accumulator for merge(), result = {} (a literal object) is used. In line 414, result[targetKey] traverses the Object.prototype chain. If Object.prototype is polluted, own keys from the polluted bucket are copied into the merged HTTP headers, thereby leaking to the outside through the HTTP request (\"ride out on the wire\"). Denial of Service Risk (lib/core/mergeConfig.js): In line 26, the hasOwnProperty descriptor is constructed as a plain object literal. Object.defineProperty follows the prototype chain when reading descriptor.get / descriptor.set. If Object.prototype.get or Object.prototype.set is polluted and returns a non-function value, it causes a synchronous TypeError to be thrown with each Axios request, resulting in a denial of service. Impact Data Leakage: Internal configurations or sensitive information may leak into network transmissions via HTTP headers. (1) lib/utils.js line 406 builds merge()s accumulator as result = {}, so result[targetKey] (line 414) walks Object.prototype and the polluted buckets own keys are copied into the merged headers and ride out on the wire. (2) lib/core/mergeConfig.js line 26 builds the hasOwnProperty descriptor as a plain-object literal. Object.defineProperty reads descriptor.get/descriptor.set via the prototype chain, so a polluted Object.prototype.get or Object.prototype.set makes the call throw TypeError synchronously on every axios request. This vulnerability is fixed in 0.32.0 and 1.16.0.
